meta.tagline: Marble streets embraced by walls, the Adriatic at their feet

pills: The real address of King's Landing

overview.title: Welcome to Dubrovnik
overview.intro: Dubrovnik is less a city than a stone ship anchored in the sea: inside two kilometers of walls the marble main street, the Stradun, gleams, and orange roof tiles compete with Adriatic blue. The Republic of Ragusa defied Venice for centuries and carried its freedom under the banner of 'Libertas' — you feel that pride in every stone today. Game of Thrones brought it new fame as King's Landing, but the real story is older: earthquakes, sieges, and marble polished anew each time. Learn the crowd's timetable, and this stone ship will sail very differently for you.

local_word.definition: Dalmatia's untranslatable state: the sweet languor of doing nothing and worrying about nothing in the midday heat. Neither laziness nor sleep — somewhere in between, drifting while gazing at the sea. Dalmatians consider fjaka a right; find a stone in the shade of the walls and claim yours.

rules.title: Walk the walls at the first hour or the last
rules.description: The wall walk is Dubrovnik's crown, but noon is both hot and crowded: go at opening or two hours before closing. The two-kilometer circuit takes one to two hours — bring water and a hat; the marble steps turn into a skillet at midday.

rules.title: Flow against the cruise-ship hours
rules.description: Ships pour thousands through the Pile Gate between 09:00 and 10:00 and collect them around 16:00: in that window, be on Lokrum or in the Lapad coves. The old town's true hours are 07:00–09:00 and after 18:00 — that's when the marble belongs to you.

rules.title: If you stay inside the walls, make peace with stairs
rules.description: The walled town is car-free and its side streets are steep staircases: you need shoulders for your suitcase and proper shoes. The reward is priceless — walking the Stradun alone at midnight is a privilege reserved for those who sleep inside.

tip.label: The Dubrovnik philosophy
tip.text: This city lives in two shifts: daytime is the shop window, morning and night are the stage. Rise early, take your fjaka at noon, swim beneath the walls at dusk — share your calendar with the light, not the crowds.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: The old town is entirely pedestrian; buses link Lapad and the port, boats add Lokrum and the islands, and the cable car adds Mount Srđ.

items.title: Arriving from the airport
items.description: Dubrovnik Airport is 30 minutes away: the shuttle bus, synced with flights, drops you near the Pile Gate. Taxis and ride apps run at fixed rates — check the return shuttle times in advance.

items.title: The pedestrian old town
items.description: No vehicles enter the walls: the Stradun is flat, the side streets are stairs. Pile and Ploče are the two main gates — the old town crosses end to end in ten minutes, yet nobody ever crosses it in ten minutes; every corner stops you.

items.title: City buses
items.description: Buses from outside the Pile Gate connect Lapad, the port of Gruž and the hotel zones: tickets from the driver or a kiosk. If you're staying outside the walls, your daily rhythm runs on these lines.

items.title: Lokrum and island boats
items.description: The Lokrum boat crosses from the old harbor to the green island in fifteen minutes; ferries from Gruž sail to the Elaphiti islands. Check the last return boat at the pier — no one stays overnight on Lokrum.

items.title: The Srđ cable car
items.description: Four minutes to the top of Mount Srđ: walls, Lokrum and the open sea in one frame. Go up an hour before sunset — and if you'd rather skip the descent queue, the path down is a half-hour feast of views.

callout.label: Pass tip
callout.text: The Dubrovnik Pass covers the wall entrance, Lovrijenac and the museums, with city buses included: even the one-day pass costs close to the wall ticket alone — if you're climbing the walls anyway, the pass almost always pays off.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: The choice is a matter of scale and staircases: stone rooms inside the walls, wall views in Ploče, beach ease in Lapad.

local_word.definition: Latin for 'freedom': the one-word constitution of the Republic of Ragusa. It was written on the flag and flew over the Minčeta tower; the city-state's merchant ships were known by it across the seas. Today it names the festival and carries the city's pride — understanding Dubrovnik begins with understanding Libertas.

items.name: Old town (inside the walls)
items.description: Rooms and small hotels in stone houses: the midnight Stradun and the empty morning squares are yours. Stairs and suitcase-hauling included — the reward is living the city at hours nobody else sees.

items.name: Ploče
items.description: Hotels outside the east gate looking back at the walls and Lokrum: Banje beach at your feet. Five minutes to the old town, postcard views — this is the honeymoon side.

items.name: Around Pile
items.description: Just outside the west gate: buses, taxis and the old town one step away. Fewer stairs, easiest transport — the smart base for a short stay.

items.name: Lapad
items.description: The peninsula's coves, a seaside promenade and a wide range of hotels: prices softer than the old town. For those who want a swimming holiday — ten minutes to the center by bus.

items.name: Cavtat
items.description: A quiet palm-lined harbor town half an hour away: the boat ride to Dubrovnik is a pleasure in itself. For those who'd rather sleep far from the crowds and visit the city as a guest.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Dubrovnik's key is managing hours more than seasons; still, May–June and September–October offer the city at its most generous.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Marble at Its Freshest
items.subtitle: Spring · Mild wall walks, a warming sea
items.description: Ideal temperatures for the wall walk, Lokrum in bloom, and a sea that turns swimmable by June: cruise traffic is lighter than summer and the light is soft for photographs. This is the city's most balanced window.

callout.label: May tip
callout.text: In May you can walk the walls even at noon — the heat is still merciful. Lokrum's peacocks and botanical paths are at their greenest this month: pack a sandwich and take your fjaka on the island.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Stage Lights
items.subtitle: Summer · Summer Festival, full Stradun, warm nights
items.description: The Dubrovnik Summer Festival turns forts and courtyards into stages, the sea is crystalline, the nights are long. Crowds and prices peak — the early-morning-and-late-evening strategy saves lives in this season.

callout.label: Midday note
callout.text: In July–August the old town is both scorching and packed from 10:00 to 16:00: give those hours to Lokrum, the Lapad coves or fjaka. Set the wall walk for opening time and your Stradun stroll for after 19:00.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: September Wisdom
items.subtitle: Autumn · Warm sea, thinning crowds
items.description: The sea holds its summer warmth, ship traffic fades, and the marble turns honey-colored in the evening light. Swimming lasts into late October — this is the season for those who want Dubrovnik both salty and serene.

callout.label: September tip
callout.text: In mid-September swim off Banje and climb the walls in the late afternoon: the stone gives back the light it stored all day. Restaurant tables need no bargaining, the cable car has no queue — the year's two smartest weeks.

items.label: Winter
items.name: The Locals' City
items.subtitle: Winter · Empty Stradun, storm-watching, the feast of St. Blaise
items.description: In winter Dubrovnik takes off its mask: the Stradun returns to the locals, storm waves crash against the walls, cafes turn to conversation. The Feast of St. Blaise (Sveti Vlaho) in early February is the city's truest day. Some restaurants close for the season — the ones that stay open are heartfelt.

callout.label: February tip
callout.text: On February 3rd, St. Blaise's Day, the city celebrates: processions, banners and prayers to its patron. On this nearly tourist-free day you see what makes Dubrovnik a city — the pride of its community.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: Dalmatian cooking is a collaboration of sea and stone oven: black risotto, Ston oysters, and peka slow-cooked under an iron bell.

local_word.definition: Meat or octopus slow-cooked for hours under an iron bell heaped with embers: Dalmatia's earth-oven ritual. A good konoba prepares peka to order — you must call a few hours ahead. The steam that rises when the bell lifts is the opening curtain of Adriatic cuisine.

items.name: Crni rižot (black risotto)
items.description: Jet-black risotto cooked in cuttlefish ink: the scent of the sea concentrated on a plate. Your lips will darken — smile; in Dalmatia that counts as a medal. Ask for grated hard cheese on top.

items.name: Ston oysters
items.description: European flat oysters grown in the channels of Ston an hour away: with lemon, on ice, fresh off the boat. The festival season falls around March — they reach Dubrovnik's counters too; ask for the 'Ston' label.

items.name: Peka
items.description: Lamb or octopus spends hours under the iron bell with potatoes: the meat turns silken, the potatoes smoky. Cooked to order — call the konoba at noon, watch the bell lift at dinner.
items.tag: To order · hours under the bell

items.name: Catch of the day at a konoba
items.description: Grilled sea bass, bream or dentex: with olive oil, garlic and blitva (chard-and-potato). Sold by the kilo — choose from the display and settle the price before the scale.

items.name: Rozata
items.description: Dubrovnik's caramel custard perfumed with rose liqueur: the local, elegant cousin of crème caramel. A cold slice to end the meal — the only dessert that carries the city's name; don't skip it.

items.name: Pelješac wines
items.description: Plavac Mali red from the peninsula's sun-baked slopes and Pošip white from Korčula: by the carafe at a konoba or in a wine bar. If you see the Dingač label, don't hesitate — it's the Adriatic's most ambitious red.
items.tag: Plavac Mali + Pošip · by the carafe

callout.label: Table rule
callout.text: On the Stradun and the wall-view terraces, the menu carries a view tax: two streets in, the same crni rižot comes at a friendly price. Wherever a 'catch of the day' question isn't answered with weight and price, don't order before seeing the scale.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone walks the Stradun and the walls; these six are the stone ship's lesser-known decks.

items.name: Buža
items.description: A bar reached through a hole in the city wall, set on the rocks: tables on the cliff, feet above the Adriatic. Signage is modest to the point of invisible — find the 'Cold drinks' sign, step through the hole, sit down for sunset.

items.name: Lokrum
items.description: Fifteen minutes by boat to another, greener world: a Benedictine monastery, peacocks, the salty 'Dead Sea' lagoon and the gardens of GoT's Qarth. The antidote to cruise hours — pack a sandwich and give the island the day.

items.name: Lovrijenac
items.description: The fort on a 37-meter rock outside the walls: they call it the 'Gibraltar of the West'. Hamlet is staged here during the Summer Festival — and the Red Keep scenes of King's Landing were shot here too. Entry is usually included with the wall ticket.

items.name: War Photo Limited
items.description: A photography gallery inside the old town telling the 1990s war and world conflicts without censorship: small, dense, shaking. Give it an hour to understand the recent history behind Dubrovnik's postcard face.

items.name: Trsteno Arboretum
items.description: A 15th-century villa garden half an hour north: giant plane trees, a pool with a Neptune fountain and terraces descending to the sea. The Red Keep gardens of GoT were filmed here — take the morning bus, be back by noon.

items.name: Gruž market and quay
items.description: Dubrovnik's daily life among morning fish stalls, fruit stands and ferry traffic: far from the old town's shop window, prices at local scale. Market breakfasts and the Elaphiti ferry both start here.

callout.label: Hour strategy
callout.text: In Dubrovnik 'when' matters as much as 'where': 07:00 wants the Stradun, noon wants Lokrum, late afternoon wants Lovrijenac, sunset wants Buža. The same places are a shop window at the wrong hour and a miracle at the right one.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: The Pearl of the Adriatic has polished its showcase games too; know these four and sail the stone ship in comfort.

items.name: The old town at cruise hour
items.description: On ship days the Stradun becomes a human river from 10:00 to 16:00: the wall-ticket queue stretches and every photo frame fills with crowds.
items.instead: Check the cruise calendar, or simply live in reverse: 07:00–09:00 and after 18:00 the city is yours. Give the peak hours to Lokrum and Lapad.

items.name: Stradun terrace prices
items.description: On the main street and some wall-view terraces, coffee and pizza multiply with a location tax; a service surprise may join the bill.
items.instead: Konobas two streets in serve the same kitchen at friendly prices; drink your coffee on the Gruž side. Never order anywhere without seeing menu prices first.

items.name: GoT tour inflation
items.description: Some walks sold under the 'King's Landing tour' label package freely walkable squares at premium prices.
items.instead: Most filming spots — the Jesuit Stairs, Lovrijenac, the Stradun — can be visited on your own; if you want a tour, choose a small group with a clear route. Prefer ones that include Trsteno.

items.name: Buying the wall ticket at noon
items.description: Using one of Europe's priciest tickets at the day's hottest, busiest hour: the shadeless marble turns the walk from joy to ordeal.
items.instead: Go at opening or two hours before closing; cover the museums too with the Dubrovnik Pass. Carry water — kiosks on the walls are few and pricey.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: Dubrovnik can be expensive, but it is not dishonest: pay for mastery, not for views. Climb the walls at the right hour, pick your konoba on a back street, and live the rest on foot and in the water — the best moments are free anyway.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Itineraries
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. Times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: From wall to water — a stone ship day

steps.title: The empty Stradun
steps.description: Walk the marble street while it belongs to no one: Onofrio's Fountain, the clock tower, the pigeons. This is the city's truest half hour.

steps.title: The wall walk
steps.description: Go at opening: from Minčeta over the sea of rooftiles, from the sea side toward Lokrum. Water and a hat with you — allow two hours.

steps.title: Lokrum escape
steps.description: Boat from the old harbor to the island: monastery gardens, peacocks and a swim in the Dead Sea lagoon. Wait out the crowded hours on the island.

steps.title: Konoba lunch-dinner
steps.description: Back in town, crni rižot or the day's fish at a back-street konoba: Pošip alongside. Claim your fjaka right here too.

steps.title: Lovrijenac and Pile cove
steps.description: Climb the fort and see the walls from across; on the way down, swim off the rocks in Pile cove — swimming beneath the walls is like nowhere else.

steps.title: Sunset at Buža
steps.description: Step through the hole in the wall, take a table on the rocks: the sun drops into the Adriatic. Close with rozata in the Stradun's evening light.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Stone ship, islands and oysters — the full Adriatic

steps.title: Classic Dubrovnik
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: empty Stradun, the walls, Lokrum, a konoba, Lovrijenac, sunset at Buža.

steps.title: Summit, memory and the harbor
steps.description: Morning cable car up Srđ and the Homeland War museum; noon at the Gruž market and a quay-side coffee; afternoon at War Photo Limited and the Rector's Palace; an evening swim off Banje with the walls in view + dinner on the Ploče side.

steps.title: Ston and Trsteno escape
steps.description: Morning bus or tour to Ston: Europe's longest defensive walls and the salt pans, lunch at an oyster counter; the Renaissance gardens of Trsteno Arboretum on the way back; farewell dinner in the old town — order your peka in the morning.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Croatian is easier to pronounce than it looks; these five phrases open the way from konoba table to market stall.

items.meaning: Good day — the foundation of every greeting entering a shop or konoba
Thank you kindly — the heartfelt version of 'hvala', delivered with a smile
Please / you're welcome — when ordering, and in reply to thanks
Enjoy your meal — the waiter says it setting down your plate; say it to your table too
Cheers! — as the Plavac Mali glasses rise; eye contact is the custom

checklist.title: Dubrovnik Checklist
checklist.completion_message: Libertas! You've lived the Pearl of the Adriatic the way it deserves!
